name: First Class
description: First Class completes the foundational outdoor skills: menu planning and serving as cook, lashings, orienteering and GPS, plants and weather, boating safety, advanced first aid, home emergency planning, citizenship and recruiting.

provenance.notes: Topic outline drafted from maintainer familiarity with the Scouts BSA rank requirements (the structure introduced in 2016 and revised since) and cross-referenced with secondary sources found by web search. Official rank requirements could not be reached from the build environment. Several sub-requirements under 1, 6 and 9 are not yet transcribed.

references.label: Wikipedia: Ranks in Scouts BSA (secondary source)

children.title: Safe food handling
children.summary: Safe handling and storage of meat, dairy, eggs, vegetables and other perishable food.
children.orientation: The USDA danger zone is 40–140 °F, where bacteria grow fastest. On a trip, that means keeping cold foods cold, not leaving perishables out too long (less time in hot weather), and cooking to safe internal temperatures checked with a food thermometer rather than by color.

children.title: Weather forecasts
children.summary: Ways to get a weather forecast and why forecasts matter when planning an activity.
children.orientation: The National Weather Service is the primary public source of U.S. forecasts and warnings. Learn the difference between a watch (conditions are favorable) and a warning (the hazard is happening or imminent), and decide ahead of time what each would mean for your trip.

children.title: Natural signs of hazardous weather
children.summary: Natural indicators that dangerous weather is approaching and what to do about it.
children.orientation: Building cumulus clouds, a sudden drop in temperature, rising wind and distant thunder are all signs to act early. Thunder means lightning is within striking distance, so move to safe shelter right away and wait until 30 minutes after the last thunder.

children.orientation: A home emergency plan covers who to contact, where to meet, how to get out, and what to do when the power or water is off. Ready.gov’s family planning guide walks through the pieces and has printable templates.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Requirement 10 is outlined from earlier official editions; its current wording was not visible in the excerpts.
